title: rapid-fidelity-lab-keisha
body:
Rapid fidelity lab — notes to self (short-form)

Context
- Quick personal scratchpad for a few odd outputs I saw while testing canary on redwood-v1-small-quant.
- Goal: capture reproducible seeds, quick ad-hoc rubric, and hypotheses to triage before filing formal bugs.
- Not a ticket yet — probable follow-ups: small sample repro, then ENG-2319 if it’s a regression.

Run details (local harness)
- model: redwood-v1-small-quant (cpu fallback), runtime: canary-2026-02
- prompt template id: prompt/faq-short-2025-v3
- params: temperature=0.0, max_tokens=120, top_p=0.95, stop_tokens=["

"]
- batch: 8 (continuous batching enabled), kv_cache warmup: none
- seed(s) I used: 42, 1337, 20251102

Samples observed (trimmed)
1) input: "How do I revoke a session token?"
   output A (good): "You can revoke a session token by calling DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}..."
   output B (weird): "You can revoke a session token by rotating your SSH key..."
   notes: B mixes infra concepts; maybe training-data contamination or prompt fallthrough. Occurred reproducibly with seed=1337, batch size 8.

2) input: "Summarize the following terms of service excerpt." (long 400 tokens)
   output: truncated mid-sentence and appended: "See also: RFC 7231"
   notes: truncation + odd external reference. Happened more when kv_cache cold and with continuous batching enabled.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick 0-2 scale)
- Correctness (0-2): 0 = wrong/confused; 1 = partial; 2 = correct/complete
- Hallucination risk (0-2): 0 = high hallucination; 2 = grounded
- Prompt-following (0-2): 0 = ignored instruction; 2 = exactly followed
- Fluency (0-2): 0 = broken; 2 = fluent

Scoring examples (for sample #1)
- A: correctness=2, hallucination=2, prompt-following=2, fluency=2 -> total 8/8
- B: correctness=0, hallucination=0, prompt-following=1, fluency=2 -> total 3/8

Quick hypotheses
- Batch mixing issue: when multiple prompts in the same batch share similar tokens, KV cache or prefix caching might bleed context. Evidence: failure freq up when batch=8 and similar subject lines in batch.
- Quantization edge-case: odd reference to RFC 7231 might be model memorized short text that's surfaced by numeric underflow in attention weights. But less likely.
- Prompt truncation path: long inputs + continuous batching could be causing token cut-offs or early EOS tokens injected by runtime.

Repro steps to produce minimal repro
1) Run single-case with seed=1337, batch=1, temperature=0.0. If B still appears -> model-only problem.
2) If not reproducible, increase batch to 8, try mixing similar subject prompts and see if B emerges.
3) Toggle continuous batching off (flag: --disable-cont-batch) and verify.
4) Try quantized vs FP16 variant (if available).

Immediate quick experiments I ran (results)
- batch=1, seed=1337 -> output A (normal). Suggests batching related.
- batch=8 with different prompts -> B observed 3/8 runs.
- batch=8, --disable-cont-batch -> mostly A. Strong signal for batching-path.

Notes to file in ticket (short bullets)
- Add reproducible script + seeds to ENG-2319.
- Include runtime logs that show request ids and per-token timings.
- Flag to SRE: any recent batching kernel change in canary-2026-02? link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-playground/pull/412

Open questions / TODOs
- Is there a per-batch token alignment bug when sequences vary in length? (priority high)
- Does KV cache warmup behavior differ when continuous batching enabled? (investigate)
- Run on dedicated GPU (non-canary) to rule out canary-only regression.

Side notes (brain dump)
- If I sketch an automated mini-check: generate 64 prompts that differ only in last token, run 100 iterations with batch 8; measure incidence of extraneous external references (RFC, Wikipedia, URLs). If incidence >> baseline, that's a good signal.
- Quick annotation plan: mark outputs as A/B, collect top tokens at divergence point, attach to ticket.

Snack-sized next steps (for my day)
- Create minimal repro script and attach to the Jira ticket (30–45m).
- Slack @marco to sanity-check if he saw similar on his canary runs.
- If repro confirmed, escalate to serving-runtime oncall and file formal regression with logs.

Endnotes
- This doc intentionally messy. Keep here until I either file ENG-2319 or close as false-positive.
